title: Exploring casino plans to enhance tourism in Pueblo, Colorado - NewsBreak
text:
By Nate Wilde ,
1 days ago
Unlike a state like Nevada that has gambling not just in casinos, but in gas stations and other businesses, casino games are only legal in a handful of towns in Colorado , including Cripple Creek, Black Hawk, and Central City.
Download the KKNN Mobile App Now However, one city’s mayor is exploring the possibility of turning another Colorado city into a casino town in an attempt to revitalize the city’s downtown area.
Will Pueblo Become Colorado’s Next Gambling Town? Pueblo, Colorado, was once the largest city in Colorado, but in recent years, it has seen a decline in safety, the economy, and the overall vibrancy of the downtown area.
Numerous businesses have closed, storefronts remain vacant, and with the exception of the Pueblo Riverwalk and a handful of restaurants and stores, there isn’t a ton of activity downtown.
However, on a recent episode of Pueblo mayor Heather Graham’s podcast ‘The Mayor’s Mixtape,’ Graham suggested that Pueblo become the next city to legalize casino gambling.
Graham did point out that her goal isn’t to make Pueblo a “casino city,” but she did suggest that opening as many as five casinos in downtown Pueblo to revitalize the area and promote tourism and nightlife.
The podcast, which was released on Tuesday, February 3, 2026, featured a conversation between Mayor Graham and a city council member by the name of Brett Boston.
Read More: Colorado Gambling Town’s Fascinating History with Donkeys
Graham made the following statement regarding the idea:
“The City of Pueblo is open for business, and we are definitely looking for new opportunities to diversify our revenue. I’m happy to hear that members of City Council like Councilor Boston are looking to attract new businesses, increase tourism and utilize our already vibrant amenities here in Pueblo which then could potentially support legalized gambling,”
Check out the full story from KRDO 13 News here.
Unsettling Things at Colorado’s Most Notoriously Haunted Cemetery WARNING: Under no circumstances should you enter this property. By doing so you risk bodily harm and/or prosecution for trespassing on private property.
Colorado’s Central City Cemetery is not only notorious for being extremely haunted, but a recent visit saw unsettling things like vandalism, pentagrams, and a small, oddly placed building with an outhouse. Grave Robbing Deterrents Found All Over Haunted Colorado Cemetery Central City, Colorado has a total of eight cemeteries, which is remarkable considering its size, with grave robbing deterrents and reputations of being haunted. Gallery Credit: Nate Wilde carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Grave Robbing Deterrents The metal structures seen here have been said to have been built in order to deter grave robbers and vandals and are found all over this particular cemetery. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Displaced Grave Stone Sadly, you see numerous displaced grave stones in the cemetery such as this one. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Died 1887 This grave, surrounded by a deterrent, marks the final resting place of someone that passed away in 1887. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Died 1848 This grave, surrounded by a deterrent, marks the final resting place of a person that passed away back in 1848. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Huge Stone This huge gravestone is one of many with deterrents built around it. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Some Have Gates Some of the deterrents, like the one seen here, have gates built into them. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube "Asleep in Jesus" This grave, which if you look closely, also has a metal deterrent, reads "Asleep in Jesus." carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Graves on the Hill Here we see some of the graves located right on the hill. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Graves in the Trees Some of the graves are surrounded by trees, while others appear to be right in the middle of them. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Steel Pole Deterrent If you look closely, you can see another grave robbing deterrent that appears to be made of metal poles. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Low Wall Here we see what appears to be a low, concrete wall surrounding a group of graves. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Benches Here we see a large gravestone with, interestingly, what appears to be stone benches. Gate Here we see one of the cemeteries' gates which look like it's seen better days. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube No Vehicles The cemetery only allows emergency and authorized vehicles, otherwise you are only allowed to visit on foot. Another Cemetery Nearby Central City has eight cemeteries in total, another of which you can see in the distance here. Stone Between Trees Here we see an unfortunate sight; a gravestone wedged between two trees. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Coins and Toys As you can see here, visitors to this grave have left things like coins and toys. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Infant Sadly, this gravestone marks the final resting place of a deceased infant. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Toy, Rocks + Guitar Pick Here we see some of the things left behind by visitors to this grave; a toy, some rocks and even an orange guitar pick. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Leaning Against a Tree Unfortunately, this headstone isn't in the ground, but rather propped up against a tree. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Toy and Rosaries Atop the gravestone is a toy and numerous rosaries. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Six Years Old Sadly, this gravestone marks, or at the very least, did mark, the final resting place of a deceased 6-year-old child. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Doll on Tree Above the grave is this doll, tied to the same tree that the gravestone was found leaning against. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Animal Digging This gravesite was not disturbed by a human, but rather an animal who, as you can see here, has done some digging. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Large Fence Here we see a section of graves protected by one of the larger deterrent fences in the cemetery. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Fenced in Trees This section of graves is not only protected by the deterrent we see here, but the fence is also surrounded by trees. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Rock Cross This gravesite is nicely decorated with rocks forming the shape of a cross. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Urn + Penny Curiously, this urn was found on a gravesite with a penny sitting on top of it. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube More Deterrents Here we see more of the structures placed to deter people from robbing or even messing with the graves in any way. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Leaning Against Tree Sadly, there are numerous gravestones not planted in the ground but merely leaning against trees in the cemetery. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Skull Symbol If you look closely, there is an odd symbol on this headstone with a skull in it. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube A.P. Oddly, this particular grave stone is really short and only reads the initials "A.P." carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Surrounded By Aspens As you can see, the cemetery is surrounded by Aspen trees. carnivorous_ghoul via YouTube Square Boundaries If you look closely, you can see four separate sections of graves with low, square boundaries. Take a Virtual Tour of Colorado's Haunted Central City Cemetery Colorado's abandoned Central City Cemetery is said to be one of the most haunted places in the state. Gallery Credit: Nate Wilde Iron Gate The cemetery is split into sections with gates leading into each one, with one seen here. Derelict Doug via YouTube Freemason Grave Here we see a Freemason Grave of a man that passed away back in 1887. Derelict Doug via YouTube Family Plots The cemetery has numerous plots of families, like the one seen here with five graves. Derelict Doug via YouTube Dog Trinket Someone left a dog trinket on the grave seen here. Derelict Doug via YouTube Displaced Headstone Unfortunately, this grave has had its headstone removed. Derelict Doug via YouTube Coking Furnace The area surrounding the cemetery was also used for mining, as we can see here there is a coking furnace in the middle of the cemetery. Derelict Doug via YouTube Civil War Vet Grave The graves are typically very old in the Central City Cemetery, as we can see here that this one is of that of a Civil War veteran. Derelict Doug via YouTube Catholic Freemason Broken Headstone One section of the cemetery was dedicated to Catholic and Freemason graves, and unfortunately one of the headstones in that section has been damaged. Derelict Doug via YouTube Circle of Branches Here's a bit of an eerie sight - a circle of branches likely put together fairly recently in the cemetery. Derelict Doug via YouTube Catholic Cemetery The Central City Cemetery is divided into sections, including a Catholic section, seen here. Derelict Doug via YouTube Wiccan Jar Here we see a jar on top of a headstone believed to be a part of a wiccan ceremony, filled with crystals and rose petals. Derelict Doug via YouTube Veteran Grave with Dreamcatcher and Flag There are many Civil War veterans buried at the Central City Cemetery, and visitors have paid their respects by leaving flags on the gravestones. However, someone also left a dreamcatcher on the gravestone seen here. Tesla Ball Because the cemetery dates back to around the same time that Nicola Tesla was living in Colorado Springs, we find what are known as 'Tesla Balls,' like the one seen here. Derelict Doug via YouTube Mining Structure Oddly enough, on the outskirts of the cemetery there was mining activity, as made evident for the ruins seen here. Derelict Doug via YouTube Knights of Pythias Another section of the Central City Cemetery was dedicated to the Knights of Pythias.
